'''Samarendra Nath Roy''' (11 December 1906&nbsp;– 23 July 1964) was an Indian-born American mathematician and an applied statistician.

==Early life==
Roy was the first of three children of [[Kali Nath Roy]] and Suniti Bala Roy.<ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1080/00031305.1964.10482640 | last1 = Bose | first1 = R. C. | year = 1964 | title = Samarendra Nath Roy, December 11, 1906 – July 23, 1964 | journal = The American Statistician | volume = 18 | issue = 5 | pages = 26–27 | jstor = 2682467}}</ref> His father, was a freedom fighter and the Chief Editor of the newspaper [[The Tribune (Chandigarh)|The Tribune]], then publishing from [[Lahore]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.tribuneindia.com/2002/tribune.htm | title = Tribuneindia...119 Years of Trust | work = [[The Tribune (Chandigarh)|The Tribune]] | accessdate = 21 January 2013 | archive-date = 7 September 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120907191419/http://www.tribuneindia.com/2002/tribune.htm | url-status = dead }}</ref> Roy and The Tribune published [https://kalinathroy.wordpress.com/kali-nath-roys-seditious-articles-1919/ seven allegedly seditious articles from April 3, 1919 through April 11, 1919], leading up to the April 13th massacre of the Indians at the hands of the British in the infamous [[Jallianwala Bagh massacre]]. For this "offence" Kali Nath Roy was sentenced to imprisonment of two years along with a fine of one thousand rupees.<ref>{{cite news | author1 = Varinder Walia | author2 = Neeraj Bagga | title = Jallianwala Bagh revisited | url = https://www.tribuneindia.com/2006/20060413/aplus.htm | access-date = 21 January 2013 | newspaper = The Tribune | date = 13 April 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | author = Gobind Thukral | title = EDITORIAL PAGE; LOOKING BACK; How 1919 Punjab rebellion was suppressed|url = https://www.tribuneindia.com/2001/20010725/edit.htm|access-date = 5 August 2013 | newspaper = The Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | author = Viscount Cave, J. | url = http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50741/ | title = Kali Nath Roy vs The King-Emperor on 9 December, 1920 | publisher = Indian Kanoon – Search engine for Indian Law | accessdate = 24 July 2013}}</ref><ref name="st-andrews1">{{cite web | url = http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Roy.html | author1 = J J O'Connor | author2 = E F Robertson | authorlink2 = Edmund F. Robertson | title = Roy Biography | publisher = [[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]] | accessdate = 21 January 2013}}</ref>

Roy secured first division in the Matriculation Examination in 1923 from the [[Khulna Zilla School|Khulna District School]].<ref name="st-andrews1"/> He was the topper in the Intermediate Science (Higher Secondary) Examinations in 1925 from the [[Brajalal College|Daulatpur Hindu Academy]].<ref name="st-andrews1"/> He obtained first class and was the topper in both the BSc Mathematics (Honours) from [[Presidency College, Kolkata|Presidency College]] of the [[University of Calcutta]] in 1928 and the MSc in Mixed Mathematics - which later was renamed to Applied Mathematics - (with The Theory of Relativity as the elective) from the renowned [[Rajabazar Science College]], [[University of Calcutta]] in 1931.<ref name=autogenerated1 /><ref name="st-andrews1"/>

==Academic career==
In 1931, when Roy joined the Department of Applied Mathematics of [[Rajabazar Science College]] at the University of Calcutta as a research associate, he used computing facilities at the newly established [[Indian Statistical Institute]],<ref name="st-andrews1"/> which was founded by Professor [[Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis|P. C. Mahalanobis]]. Roy along with several talented young scholars including [[J. M. Sengupta]], [[H. C. Sinha]], [[Raj Chandra Bose]], K. R. Nair, [[K. Kishen]] and [[C. R. Rao]], joined to form an active group of statisticians under Mahalanobis. Roy was one of the very early students of Mahalanobis, who initiated some of the early works in Statistics.<ref name="mudholkar">{{cite journal | title = Life and legacy of Samarendra Nath Roy 1906–1964 | journal = Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference | volume = 137 | issue = 11 | pages = 3208–3212 | author1 = Govind S. Mudholkar | author2 = Alan D. Hutsonb | author3 = Michael P. McDermotta | doi = 10.1016/j.jspi.2007.03.003 | year = 2007 }}</ref> He was well known for his pioneering contribution to multivariate statistical analysis, mainly that of the Jacobians of complicated transformations for various exact distributions, rectangular coordinates and the Bartlett decomposition.<ref>{{cite web | last = V. Mardia | first = Kanti | title = On S.N. Roy's Legacy to Multivariate Analysis | url = http://www.maths.leeds.ac.uk/statistics/research/reports/2007/STAT07-07.pdf | work = Presented as a plenary talk to S. N. Roy Multivariate Conference, Kolkata (December 2006) | accessdate = 26 October 2012 | date = 23 January 2008 | archive-date = 29 July 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120729141026/http://www1.maths.leeds.ac.uk/statistics/research/reports/2007/STAT07-07.pdf | url-status = dead }}</ref> His dissertation included the Post master's work at the Indian Statistical Institute where he worked under Mahalanobis.<ref name="snr-mgenealogy1">{{MathGenealogy|id=29412}}</ref>

It was Bose who first went to the United States as a visiting professor at [[Columbia University]] and then joined the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] in 1947. Roy followed suit by later joining him at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] in the spring of 1950, after initially travelling to the United States to take up a Visiting Professorship of Statistics at [[Columbia University in New York]] in the spring of 1949. In between this Roy returned to India and became Head of the Department of Statistics at the [[University of Calcutta]] during the academic year 1949–50.<ref name="st-andrews1"/> Roy joined Bose as full Professor of Statistics in the Statistics Department at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. S. N. Roy had 15 doctorate students there from 1950 till 1963.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.stat.unc.edu/phds.html#1950 | title = PhDs Awarded | publisher = Department of Statistics and Operations Research, [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] | accessdate = 21 January 2013 | archive-date = 24 January 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180124015030/http://www.stat.unc.edu/phds.html#1950 | url-status = dead }}</ref> To commemorate his Birth Centenary an International Conference on "Multivariate Statistical Methods in the 21st Century: The Legacy of Prof. S.N. Roy" was held at Kolkata, India during 28–29 December 2006.<ref>{{cite web | title = Multivariate Statistical Methods in the 21st Century: The Legacy of Prof. S.N. Roy | url = http://www.isical.ac.in/~multstatconf/ | year = 2006 | publisher = Indian Statistical Institute | accessdate = 18 February 2013}}</ref> The Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference published a special issue for celebrating the Centennial of Birth of S. N. Roy.<ref name="mudholkar"/>

==Personal life==
Roy was married to [[Bani Roy]] and had four children, Prabir, Subir, Tapon and Sunanda. He died while on holiday in Jasper, Canada.

==Selected publications==
* Potthoff, R. F. and Roy, S. N. (1964), "A generalized multivariate analysis of variance model useful especially for growth curve problems", Biometrika, vol. 51, pp.&nbsp;313–326.
* Roy, S. N. (1957), "Some Aspects of Multivariate Analysis", New York: Wiley.
* Roy, S. N. and Sarhan, A. E. (1956), "On inverting a class of patterned matrices", Biometrika, 43, 227–231.

==Selected Ph.D. dissertations under Roy's guidance==
* [[Ingram Olkin|Olkin, Ingram]] (1951). "On distribution problems in [[multivariate analysis]]".
* Pachares, James (1953). "On the distribution of [[quadratic forms]]".
* Pillai, K.C. Sreedharan (1954). "On some distribution problems in [[multivariate analysis]]".
* Mitra, Sujit Kumar (1956).<ref>{{ cite journal | journal = Current Science | volume = 87 | issue = 3 | year = 2004 | page = 395 | url = http://www.iisc.ernet.in/currsci/aug102004/395.pdf | first = P | last = Bhimasankaram | title = Sujit Kumar Mitra (1932–2004)}}</ref> "Contributions to the statistical analysis of [[categorical data]]".
* Gnanadesikan, Ramanathan (1957). "Contributions to [[multivariate analysis]] including [[univariate]] and multivariate [[variance]] [[components analysis]] and [[factor analysis]]".
* Potthoff, Richard F. (1958). "Multi-dimensional incomplete block designs".
* Diadmond, Earl L. (1958). "Asymptotic power and independence of certain classes of tests on categorical data".
* Bargman, Rolf (1958). "A study of independence and dependence in multivariate normal analysis".
* Cobb, Whitfield (1959). "Studies in univariate and multivariate variance components analysis connected with sampling from a finite population".
* Bhapkar, Vasant P. (1959). "Contributions to the statistical analysis of experiments with one or more responses".
* Sathe, Yashawande S. (1962). "Studies in certain types of nonparametric inference".
* Das Gupta, Somesh (1963). "Some problems in classification".
* Mudholkar, Govind S. (1963). "Some contributions to the theory of univariate and multivariate statistical analysis".
Sources:<ref name="mudholkar"/><ref name="snr-mgenealogy1"/><ref>{{cite web | publisher = The Department of Statistics and Operations Research at UNC | title = PhDs awarded | url = http://www.stat.unc.edu/phds.html | access-date = 7 November 2006 | archive-date = 24 January 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180124015030/http://www.stat.unc.edu/phds.html | url-status = dead }}</ref>

==Recognition==
* Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]
* Fellow of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 1951
* President of the Statistical Section of the [[Indian Science Congress]] in 1948
* Fellow of The National Institute of Sciences (FNASc), India (now known as the [[Indian National Science Academy]]) in 1946
